arguments.title: Card plan for the Warehouse Stock Ledger
arguments.spec:
- This is a planning job: the deliverable is `plan/cards.json`, a dependency-linked set of cards an implementation team would pick up for the Warehouse Stock Ledger (`input/specification.md`) -- never write, scaffold, or stub the service itself; no implementation code belongs in this workspace.
- Referential integrity: every `dependsOn` id is a declared card (no self-deps); every `coversObligations` id is an obligation the specification declares (OBL-01..OBL-20); every card covers at least one obligation.
- Sizing: at most three entries in `filesLikelyTouched` per card, and no two cards may claim the same file.
- Module ownership: every obligation names its module as `[module: <path>]`. For every obligation a card covers, that card's filesLikelyTouched must include that exact module path. Obligations sharing a module (four name src/stock/quantity.js) must be covered by the SAME card, because only one card may own that file -- a one-obligation-per-card plan cannot satisfy both this rule and the sizing rule at once.
- Acyclicity: the dependency graph must be a DAG.
- Edge-list agreement: `dependencies` must contain exactly the edges the cards' `dependsOn` imply -- no more, no fewer.
- Testability honesty: a card whose `filesLikelyTouched` contains no test-shaped path MUST be `not_testable`; a card that does touch one MUST be `testable`.
- Coverage: only checked once `"complete": true` is set, at which point every one of the twenty obligations (OBL-01..OBL-20) must be covered by some card.
- `input/specification.md` is frozen evidence (content-hashed every run) -- never edit it.
- Acceptance is the same command for both deliverable states: `npm test`, offline, no new dependencies.
arguments.plan:
1. Card `draft-card-plan` writes the full `plan/cards.json`: eleven cards, one per module named in the specification's `[module: <path>]` annotations -- quantity and location arithmetic first (no deps), the ledger on top of both, reservations and cycle-counting on the ledger, replenishment on reservations, the API endpoints (receipts, picks, adjustments) on the modules they call, valuation reporting on the ledger, and audit last (depending on every mutating module). Each card's filesLikelyTouched anchors the exact module path every obligation it covers names, so no two cards fight over a file and the module-ownership rule holds by construction. `complete` stays false.
2. Card `verify-plan-coverage` (depends on `draft-card-plan`) re-checks that all twenty obligations (OBL-01..OBL-20) are covered by some card, THEN flips `complete` to true. `npm test` must be green at 11/11 for this final state.
arguments.summary: Turn the Warehouse Stock Ledger service specification into an eleven-card dependency-linked implementation plan (plan/cards.json), one card per module (quantity, location, ledger, reservation, cyclecount, replenish, receipts, picks, adjustments, valuation, audit) so obligations sharing a module land on the same card and stay within the sizing and file-ownership rules. Two chained cards: draft the full plan first, then verify coverage and flip complete to true. No service code is written; the plan is the deliverable.

tasks.title: Draft the full eleven-card implementation plan, grouped by module
tasks.prompt:
Write `plan/cards.json` only -- the full card plan, in one pass. Do not write, scaffold or stub any service code; no implementation code from `input/specification.md` belongs in this workspace. This is a planning job, not a build job.

Read `input/specification.md` (twenty obligations, OBL-01..OBL-20, each annotated `[module: <path>]`) before writing a single card. Start from the MODULES, not the obligation list: group every obligation that names the same module onto one card. Four obligations name src/stock/quantity.js and must be one card's work; mirroring obligations one-to-one into cards cannot satisfy both the sizing rule (at most 3 files per card, no two cards sharing a file) and module ownership (a card covering an obligation must list that obligation's exact module path in filesLikelyTouched) at the same time.

The eleven modules and their obligations: src/stock/quantity.js (OBL-01..04), src/stock/location.js (OBL-05, OBL-06), src/stock/ledger.js (OBL-07..09), src/stock/reservation.js (OBL-10, OBL-11), src/stock/cyclecount.js (OBL-13, OBL-14), src/stock/replenish.js (OBL-12), src/api/receipts.js (OBL-15), src/api/picks.js (OBL-16), src/api/adjustments.js (OBL-17), src/report/valuation.js (OBL-18, OBL-19), src/audit/trail.js (OBL-20). One card per module, each pairing its module file with its own test file (two files per card, well within the 1-3 limit) -- that pairing is also what keeps testability honest (testable, since every card touches a test-shaped path).

Dependency order follows the design: quantity and location first (no deps, pure arithmetic), the ledger on top of both, reservations and cycle-counting on the ledger, replenishment on reservations (it triggers off available-to-promise), the API endpoints on the modules they call (receipts on location+ledger, picks on reservation, adjustments on ledger), valuation reporting on the ledger, and audit last, depending on every mutating module (receipts, picks, adjustments, cyclecount, reservation).

Referential integrity: every `dependsOn` id is a declared card (no self-deps); every `coversObligations` id is an obligation the specification declares; every card covers at least one obligation.

Edge-list agreement: `dependencies` must contain exactly the edges the cards' `dependsOn` imply -- one `{"from": "<card>", "to": "<card>"}` per `dependsOn` entry, no more, no fewer.

Leave `"complete": false` -- the coverage-completeness pass is the next card's job.

Non-goals: do not set `complete: true`; do not edit `input/specification.md`, `test/**`, or `scripts/run-tests.mjs` (frozen evidence); do not write any actual service source file -- `filesLikelyTouched` paths are planned, not created.

Acceptance: `npm test` must pass (all structural checks, including module ownership, hold regardless of `complete`).

Re-derive the obligation list from `input/specification.md` (OBL-01..OBL-20) and confirm every one is named in some card's `coversObligations`, and that each covering card's `filesLikelyTouched` includes that obligation's exact `[module: <path>]`. If anything is missing, fix the plan (still respecting sizing, no file collisions, module ownership, and testability honesty) before declaring completion.

Once every obligation is covered, set `"complete": true`.

Non-goals: do not edit `input/specification.md`, `test/**`, or `scripts/run-tests.mjs` (frozen evidence); do not write any actual service source file.

Acceptance: `npm test` must pass, including the coverage check that only runs once `complete` is true.
